name: Freie Weingärtner Wachau / Domäne Wachau Riesling Smaragd Loibenberg 2022
text:
## Domäne Wachau Riesling Smaragd Ried Loibenberg 2022

**The story.** Domäne Wachau (listed in your cellar as Freie Weingärtner Wachau / Domäne Wachau) is a growers' cooperative in the [Wachau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wachau), the steep, terraced stretch of the [Danube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danube) valley in Lower Austria. It calls itself "a next generation co-op": its growers each farm less than two hectares on average, mostly by hand, and it is Austria's leading estate for organically farmed vineyards. It is run by Roman Horvath MW and Heinz Frischengruber, and its home is a Baroque cellar palace in the [Wachau](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Dom%C3%A4ne+Wachau,+Wachau,+Austria&t=k) ([Domäne Wachau](https://www.domaene-wachau.at/en/); [Domäne Wachau, 2022 Loibenberg sheet](https://www.domaene-wachau.at/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/DW-Riesling-Smaragd-Loibenberg-2022-e.pdf)).

**The valley.** The Wachau is a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape (since 2000), between Melk and Krems. People have lived there since the Stone Age: figurines found at Galgenberg and Willendorf are 32,000 and 26,000 years old. Its monasteries terraced the slopes for vines from the 9th century onwards ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wachau)).

**The vineyard: Loibenberg.** Loibenberg is one of Austria's "grand crus": more than 20 hectares of terraces held up by dry-stone walls, some dating from the 14th century, rising to 420 metres. The soil is weathered Gföhl gneiss with patches of loess and loam, and warm Pannonian air makes it the "hotplate" of the Wachau. Domäne Wachau's Riesling grows on especially high parcels with very poor soil and low yields; it is hand-picked in several passes, given a few hours on the skins, and fermented in steel ([Domäne Wachau](https://www.domaene-wachau.at/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/DW-Riesling-Smaragd-Loibenberg-2022-e.pdf)).

**Smaragd.** Smaragd is the Wachau's term for its dry, dense and complex wines, which combine structure and depth with great ageing potential ([Domäne Wachau](https://www.domaene-wachau.at/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/DW-Riesling-Smaragd-Loibenberg-2022-e.pdf)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [Austria vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/austria) says 2022 began with a dry winter and late budding; rain at flowering brought coulure and mildew, then the summer was hot and very dry until 20 August, when the rain returned. Riesling, ripening later than Grüner Veltliner, could often hang longer. The estate adds that September was a fight with the rain, but October brought sunshine and slow, ideal ripening, and wines "of energy and tension" ([Domäne Wachau](https://www.domaene-wachau.at/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/DW-Riesling-Smaragd-Loibenberg-2022-e.pdf)).

**What the critics say for 2022.** As listed by the estate ([Domäne Wachau](https://www.domaene-wachau.at/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/DW-Riesling-Smaragd-Loibenberg-2022-e.pdf)):
- **Falstaff: 94.**
- **[Vinous](https://vinous.com): 94.**
- **[Wine Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wine_Advocate): 93.**
- **[Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson): 17/20.**
- **À la Carte: 95.**
- Your CellarTracker list has no community score for this wine yet.

The estate's own note: ripe stone fruit, orange zest and lime on the nose; tropical fruit, ripe mango and pineapple on the palate, with salty, mineral notes and lively acidity. "A true powerhouse among the wines of the Wachau."

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is four years old, and your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2026 to 2034. It is just opening: still taut and fruity, with years ahead. Drink one now if you're curious, but it will gain depth over the next five years. Serve at 10 to 12°C, not ice-cold.

**Food.** The estate suggests fried branzino with asparagus risotto, a seafood pizza, Viennese boiled beef ([Tafelspitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tafelspitz)) with apple horseradish, or a spicy Indian fish curry ([Domäne Wachau](https://www.domaene-wachau.at/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/DW-Riesling-Smaragd-Loibenberg-2022-e.pdf)).

**Value and where to buy.** The next vintage is on the shelves: BSW Liquor has the Loibenberg Smaragd Riesling 2023 at $53.99, and ZYN at $50.

**Curious details**
- **A captive king.** Above the town of Dürnstein stands the castle where [Richard the Lionheart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_I_of_England) was imprisoned by Duke Leopold V on his way home from the Crusades. He was freed only on payment of an enormous ransom in silver ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wachau)).
- **World's best.** Domäne Wachau was ranked number 3 in the World's Best Vineyards list (and number 1 in Europe) in 2020 ([Domäne Wachau](https://www.domaene-wachau.at/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/DW-Riesling-Smaragd-Loibenberg-2022-e.pdf)).
